notes.publicDescription: Hoody Notes: notebooks, pages and databases in the browser. Whether a framed Notes page shares its local cache with Notes open in a tab depends on the browser: a frame embedded by another site usually gets separate storage. Separate caches exchange changes, offline edits included, once they sync with the server. Offline edits survive a reload only when the browser gives Notes persistent storage; where it does not, Notes runs from memory and unsynced edits are lost on reload.

display.client.label: Display
display.client.publicDescription: Opens the display in the web viewer.

decorations.publicDescription: Show window title bars and buttons. Set false for a frameless look.

toolbar.publicDescription: Show the toolbar. false hides it, exactly as menu=false does.

menu.publicDescription: Show the menu button. false hides it, exactly as toolbar=false does.

maximize_new_windows.publicDescription: Open new application windows maximized. On by default; off by default when decorations is false or 0, since a window without a title bar has nothing to restore it from. Set false to keep the centred placement. On a desktop smaller than 1024 pixels in either direction new windows fill the screen whatever this says; dialogs, menus and fixed-size windows are never maximized.

readonly.publicDescription: View-only mode: keyboard and mouse input is not sent.

colorScheme.publicDescription: Colour scheme of the viewer: `light`, `dark`, or `system` to follow the device. The default is `system`. If dark_mode is also set, `system` wins over it and `dark_mode=true` wins over `light`.

theme.publicDescription: Colour theme of the viewer interface. The default is `oc-1`.

font.publicDescription: Font family of the viewer interface, by name, for example `Inter` or `IBM Plex Mono`. Letters, digits, spaces, underscores and hyphens only. A name the browser cannot find falls back to Inter. By default the viewer uses its own font.

encoding.publicDescription: Encoding the viewer asks the server to use for window updates. Defaults to `webp`, which keeps text sharp. `auto` lets the server choose, and it may switch busy windows to a video encoding that looks blurry. The server only uses an encoding that both ends support.

quality_mode.publicDescription: How the viewer picks image quality, the same choice as the Image Quality menu. `auto` (the default) uses full quality and switches to a lower one while the connection is detected as slow, then back; each switch reconnects the viewer, so it needs reconnect to be on (with reconnect off the viewer stays at full quality). `best` always uses full quality. `reduced` uses a lower quality, for picture formats that have one: png, rgb and avif encodings stay as they are. Any other value counts as `auto`. A fixed quality overrides it.

quality.publicDescription: Fixed image quality for this viewer, 0 to 100. Unset, quality_mode decides, and a fixed quality wins over it. It also hides the Image Quality choice in the menu. Lossless encodings (png, rgb) ignore it.

offscreen.publicDescription: Decode and paint in a Web Worker (offscreen canvas). On by default in Chrome and Chromium over https and in Firefox 108 or later; never on Safari or other WebKit browsers, where it stays off even if you ask for it. false turns it off.

scroll.publicDescription: Let the server send region copies instead of new pixels when a window scrolls, which keeps scrolling smooth. On by default except in Safari. Without this parameter the viewer offers it only to a server it has already found safe for it, and only with reconnect on; true or false forces the choice.

bandwidth_limit.publicDescription: Bandwidth limit for this viewer in bits per second; 0 means unlimited.

override_width.publicDescription: Width in pixels of the desktop the viewer asks for; the page scales it to fit the window. `auto` (the default) uses the window's own width.

vrefresh.publicDescription: Screen refresh rate in Hz sent to the server. Unset, or -1, the viewer measures it and uses 60 when it cannot.

suspend_inactive_tab.publicDescription: Pause updates while the browser tab is hidden.

sound.publicDescription: Play the session's audio in the viewer.

keyboard.publicDescription: Show the on-screen keyboard from the start. On by default in mobile browsers and off elsewhere; the keyboard button in the menu opens and closes it either way.

swap_keys.publicDescription: Swap the Ctrl and Cmd (Meta) keys. On by default on macOS and off elsewhere.

scroll_speed.publicDescription: Scroll speed multiplier for a mouse wheel. 1 is normal. The default is 1; the page keeps it between 0.2 and 3.

touchpad_scroll_scale.publicDescription: Scroll speed multiplier for a touchpad. Lower values make scrolling less sensitive. The default is 0.85; the page keeps it between 0.2 and 2.

clipboard.publicDescription: Set false to turn clipboard sharing off for this viewer.

clipboard_poll.publicDescription: Set false to stop the viewer polling your local clipboard for changes to send to the session. Polling is on by default, except in Firefox, and in Safari over https.

printing.publicDescription: Set false to turn print forwarding off.

file_transfer.publicDescription: Set false to turn file transfer off.

display_notifications.publicDescription: Show notifications inside the display view.

reconnect.publicDescription: Reconnect automatically after a lost connection.

reconnect_count.publicDescription: How many quick reconnect attempts the viewer makes after a connection that worked is lost, before it stops. The default is 30. Needs reconnect to be on.

soft_giveup_attempts.publicDescription: Failed attempts to reach a display that has not connected yet before the viewer reports that it cannot connect and moves to slow retries. The default is 30. The time limit soft_giveup_ms counts too, whichever comes first.

soft_giveup_ms.publicDescription: Milliseconds of failed attempts to reach a display that has not connected yet before the viewer reports that it cannot connect and moves to slow retries. The default is 90000.

slow_retry_delay.publicDescription: Milliseconds between the slow retries that follow that report. The default is 15000.

slow_retry_max_ms.publicDescription: Milliseconds, counted from the first attempt, after which a viewer that has never connected stops its slow retries and closes. It is checked only once the first-connection give-up (soft_giveup_attempts, soft_giveup_ms) has happened, and does not apply after a connection that worked is lost (reconnect_count covers that). 0 removes this limit only. The default is 1200000 (20 minutes).

floating_menu.publicDescription: Show the floating menu. false hides it together with the menu button.

scroll_reverse_y.publicDescription: Reverse vertical scrolling: auto, true or false.

title_show_hoody.publicDescription: Show Hoody in the page title.

title_show_display_id.publicDescription: Show the display number in the page title.

record.publicDescription: Start recording the display in the browser about two seconds after the recorder is ready, which is after the viewer has painted the display for the first time (or 4 seconds after it began waiting for that paint, if nothing paints). mp4 and webm recordings normally stream to a browser download; some browsers download only after recording stops, and if the viewer falls back to buffering, use its Download menu after stopping. A gif downloads automatically after rendering. See record_format, record_codec and record_fps. The default is off.

record_format.publicDescription: File format of the recording started by record: `mp4`, `webm` or `gif`. The default is `mp4`.

record_codec.publicDescription: Video codec of the recording: `h264` or `h265` for mp4, `vp8` or `vp9` for webm. The default is `h264` for mp4 and `vp9` (else `vp8`) for webm. A codec the format or the browser does not support is replaced by another codec of the same format when the browser has one; when it has none (no mp4 codec, or no webm support), recording does not start and the viewer does not switch to another format. gif has no codec.

record_fps.publicDescription: Frames per second of the recording, 1 to 60. The default is 30, or 10 for gif.

parent_keys.publicDescription: Hand two keyboard chords to the page that frames the viewer: Ctrl+Alt+B and Ctrl+Alt with an arrow key are not sent to the display, and that page receives a hoody-parent-key message naming the chord (escape, left, right, up or down), sent only to its own origin. Without a framing page the keys work as usual.

parent_origin.publicDescription: The origin of the page that frames the viewer, such as https://app.example.com, for parent_keys. Used when the browser sends no referrer naming that page. The viewer keeps the origin it uses in its own address, so its own reloads and reconnects keep reaching that page. Ignored unless it is an http or https origin.

notes.uploads.label: Uploads
notes.uploads.publicDescription: Opens the uploads list of a notebook.

userId.publicDescription: Your own user id in the notebook to open, as the viewing identity knows it (not the notebook id, and not another member's user id: an id the viewer does not have opens Notes home instead). New ids are 24 lowercase hexadecimal characters; older ids may be up to 28 lowercase letters and digits.

mode.publicDescription: Share presentation. Either value hides the sidebar. readonly shows the notebook's content and management views as a viewer sees them; your own account settings and appearance preferences stay editable. readwrite keeps the editing controls your permissions allow, including section and channel role overrides. Neither changes permissions.

sidebar.publicDescription: Set to hidden to hide the notebook sidebar.

colorScheme.publicDescription: Light or dark colour scheme, over the saved preference. A page set to light or dark in its own appearance keeps it.
